artistic-culture-in-the-french-speaking-.d: Artistic Culture in the French-speaking World
terms: La chanson
French song traditions, from classic chanteurs like Brassens to modern rap and slam, expressing cultural and political ideas.
La francophonie culturelle
The shared artistic and linguistic culture uniting French-speaking communities worldwide through music, film, literature and art.
La littérature francophone
Writing in French from Africa, the Caribbean and Quebec as well as France, voicing diverse identities and experiences.
Le cinéma
French and francophone film, from the Nouvelle Vague to modern auteurs, often used to explore social and historical themes.
Le patrimoine
The cultural heritage of France and francophone regions, including monuments, museums and UNESCO sites, which shapes national and regional identity.
Les festivals
Major cultural festivals such as the Festival de Cannes or the Fête de la Musique that celebrate and promote francophone arts.

aspects-of-french-speaking-society-curre.d: Aspects of French-speaking Society: Current Issues
terms: Conditional perfect
Would have done: aurais/aurait/auraient + past participle. Used in counterfactuals.
L'immigration
Migration into a country, often discussed in relation to asile (asylum) and integration.
L'intégration
The process of becoming part of the host society; linked to citoyenneté (citizenship).
La régularisation
Process by which undocumented migrants obtain legal status — debated under successive French governments.
Le sans-papiers
Undocumented immigrant ('without papers'); politically charged term in France.
Subjunctive triggers
Mood used after il faut que, je veux que, bien que, pour que, sans que, à condition que.

aspects-of-french-speaking-society-curre.d: Aspects of French-speaking Society: Current Trends
terms: Future tense
Stem + ai/as/a/ons/ez/ont: 'le président changera la loi'.
L'Assemblée nationale
Lower house with 577 députés elected for 5 years from single-member constituencies.
La Cinquième République
Fifth Republic established by de Gaulle in 1958; semi-presidential system.
La cohabitation
When the president and prime minister come from opposing parties — has occurred three times since 1986.
Le président de la République
Head of state elected for 5 years (quinquennat) since 2002; currently chosen by direct universal suffrage.
Les gilets jaunes
Yellow vests movement, started November 2018 against fuel tax rises and the cost of living.

aspects-of-political-life-in-the-french-.d: Aspects of Political Life in the French-speaking World
terms: L'Afrique subsaharienne francophone
Includes Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, Mali, Cameroon — official French alongside national languages.
La colonisation
French colonial empire reached its peak in the early 20th century; decolonisation accelerated 1956–62.
La francophonie
Community of French-speaking countries; the Organisation internationale de la Francophonie has 88 member states.
Le Maghreb
North-west Africa: Algeria, Morocco, Tunisia — colonised by France and a major source of post-war immigration.
Le Québec
French-speaking province of Canada; Law 101 (1977) made French the sole official language.
Le créole
Creole languages spoken in Haiti, Martinique, Guadeloupe, Réunion — French-based but distinct.
L'esprit critique
Critical thinking: weighing different viewpoints and evaluating the reliability of sources rather than accepting them uncritically.
La bibliographie
The list of sources consulted, allowing the work to be verified and showing the breadth of research undertaken.
La problématique
The focused research question that guides the Individual Research Project and must be answerable through analysis rather than simple description.
La présentation orale
The spoken defence of the project in the speaking exam, where the student explains findings and responds to questions in French.
La synthèse
Drawing together findings from several sources into a coherent argument that answers the research question.
Les sources
Books, articles, films and websites in French used as evidence, which must be reliable, relevant and properly referenced.
L'analyse critique
Critical analysis: examining how techniques and choices create meaning, rather than just retelling the story.
L'intrigue
The plot: the sequence of events and conflicts that structure the narrative of a literary text or film.
La citation
A short quotation from the text used as evidence to support analytical points in an essay.
La mise en scène
In film, the arrangement of setting, lighting, framing and acting that the director uses to create meaning.
Le personnage
A character whose development, motives and relationships reveal the work's meaning and the author's or director's intentions.
Le thème
A central idea explored in a set text or film, such as freedom, memory or social injustice, which students analyse with evidence.
Justifier son opinion
Backing up opinions with reasons and examples, using phrases like 'à mon avis' and 'parce que', to gain higher marks.
La prononciation
Clear pronunciation and intonation, including nasal vowels and the silent final consonants typical of French.
La spontanéité
Responding naturally to unexpected questions, showing fluency rather than reciting a memorised script.
Le débat
A structured spoken discussion where the student defends a viewpoint, gives reasons and responds to counter-arguments in French.
Le registre
Choosing an appropriate level of formality, including correct use of 'vous', for the speaking exam context.
Les connecteurs
Connectives such as 'd'une part', 'cependant' and 'par conséquent' that link ideas and make spoken answers flow logically.

unit-2-listening-reading-and-use-of-fren.d: Unit 2: Listening, Reading and Use of French
terms: François Truffaut
Director of Les Quatre Cents Coups (1959), a semi-autobiographical New Wave landmark.
Intouchables (2011)
Olivier Nakache & Éric Toledano's box-office hit about class and disability in contemporary France.
Jean-Luc Godard
Director of À bout de souffle (1960), known for jump cuts and political experimentation.
La Nouvelle Vague
French New Wave (late 1950s–60s); directors Truffaut, Godard, Chabrol broke with studio conventions.
Le cinéma d'auteur
Auteur cinema — director-driven film where the filmmaker is treated as the principal author.
Past historic (passé simple)
Literary past tense used in narration: 'il alla, elle vit, ils furent'.

unit-3-extended-writing-film-and-literat.d: Unit 3: Extended Writing - Film and Literature
terms: Albert Camus
Algerian-born French writer (1913–60); Nobel laureate 1957; key figure of absurdism.
Imperfect for description
Imparfait used for backgrounds and habitual actions: 'il faisait chaud, le soleil brûlait'.
L'absurde
The absurd — Camus's central idea: the conflict between human search for meaning and a silent universe.
L'Étranger (1942)
Camus's novel narrated by Meursault, whose emotional detachment leads to his condemnation for murder.
La Peste (1947)
Allegorical novel set in Oran during a plague; widely read as a metaphor for the Occupation.
Le Mythe de Sisyphe (1942)
Philosophical essay arguing one must imagine Sisyphus happy despite the absurdity of his task.

unit-4-as-themes-relationships;-culture-.d: Unit 4: AS Themes (Relationships; Culture and Lifestyle)
terms: La famille recomposée
Blended family — formed after divorce/remarriage; increasingly common in France since the 1980s.
La parentalité
Parenthood — covers shared roles of mothers and fathers; congé parental is parental leave.
Le PACS
Pacte civil de solidarité — civil union introduced in 1999, open to same-sex and opposite-sex couples.
Le divorce
Divorce — roughly 45% of French marriages end in divorce; consensual divorce was simplified in 2017.
Le mariage pour tous
Same-sex marriage legalised in France in 2013 under the Taubira law.
Reflexive verbs (pronominaux)
Verbs like se marier, s'entendre, se disputer that take être in the passé composé and agree with the subject.

terms: L'engagement
Civic and political engagement, including volunteering ('le bénévolat'), protest and voting, through which young people shape society.
L'immigration
The movement of people into France and francophone countries, raising questions of identity, opportunity and social cohesion.
L'intégration
Integration: the process by which newcomers become part of society, debated alongside ideas of assimilation and multiculturalism.
La mondialisation
Globalisation: the growing interconnection of economies and cultures, affecting jobs, identity and the French language worldwide.
Le multiculturalisme
A society made up of many cultures living together, a key theme in debates about France's changing identity.
Les jeunes
Young people in society: their values, education, employment prospects and political engagement in the French-speaking world.

theme-4-the-occupation-and-the-resistanc.d: Theme 4: The Occupation and the Resistance
terms: L'Occupation
The period 1940–1944 when Nazi Germany occupied France after the defeat of June 1940, dividing the country into zones.
L'appel du 18 juin
General de Gaulle's radio appeal from London in June 1940 urging the French to continue fighting; a founding moment of la France libre.
La Libération
The liberation of France in 1944, including the Normandy landings and the freeing of Paris in August 1944.
La Résistance
The networks of French people who fought the occupation through sabotage, intelligence and the underground press.
La collaboration
Cooperation by some French individuals and the Vichy regime with the Nazi occupiers, including in the persecution of Jews.
Le régime de Vichy
The collaborationist French government led by Marshal Pétain from 1940, based in Vichy in the unoccupied southern zone.
